done.why: I had the egg in the trophy case by turn 17, which was what I came for. I went underground afterwards to look around, killed the troll and got as far as the Dome Room. Then the trap door was barred behind me and I was carrying no rope, and the rest of the map clearly goes on a long way, so I stopped there.

about: It's a reworked version of the white-house treasure hunt. You break into an abandoned house, find treasures in the woods and under the ground, and bring them back to a trophy case that's waiting to be filled. The new descriptions give ordinary objects a bit of wit and sometimes a quiet hint, like a railing that's basically asking you to tie something to it.

ending.what: I put the jewel-encrusted egg in the trophy case (turn 17). The score went to 20 out of 350, and 'look in case' listed the egg as my collection.

moments.note: I climbed the tree and the egg was right there, described in loving, fragile detail.
The nest description is funny: 'better taste in treasure than in architecture.'
The trophy case 'has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.' It nudged me toward the goal nicely.
The goal took 17 moves and the egg never broke. That was easier than I expected.
The gothic door reads 'This space intentionally left blank.'
The trap door slammed shut and someone barred it, so I was cut off from the house.
A tense troll fight. I got stunned, then knocked him out and he vanished in black fog.
The railing description almost tells you to tie a rope to it. A clever, gentle hint.
The thief wandered through and left empty-handed. I was glad the egg was already locked away.

wished: Go back up and check the egg was still safe in the case after the thief turned up, but the trap door had been barred behind me
Find a rope to get down from the Dome Room
Open the egg's delicate clasp. I never tried it because I didn't want to break it

lines.line: wedged into the fork of a branch by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.
lines.why: It's funny and gives the nest some character.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: It told me where the treasures go without saying it outright.

lines.line: the sort of thing a careful person makes something fast to before trusting the drop. It is the most reassuring thing you have seen in some time.
lines.why: A hint about rope worked into the description.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: Ominous. Suddenly I was committed to the underground.

fun.why: Getting the egg felt good, and the troll fight and the thief made the trip underground lively.

engagement.why: After the goal was done I kept going because each new room or object had something worth reading.

difficulty.why: The goal took 17 moves, with no puzzle in the way. The egg didn't break and the case opened straight away.

interestingness.why: The added descriptions use the scenery to hint at puzzles, like the railing and the case. It made me want to examine everything.

prose.why: The new descriptions are warm, witty and precise, and they fit well with the original terse style.
